definitions.gloss: slow and fast; pace variation; modulation
definitions.explanation: the variation between slow and fast speeds or tempos; used in music, speech, and sports
a critical or pressing situation requiring immediate action (used in the expression 緩急の際)

examples.japanese: {演奏|えんそう}に{緩急|かんきゅう}をつけることで{表現|ひょうげん}が{豊|ゆた}かになる。
examples.english: Adding tempo variation to the performance makes the expression richer.

examples.japanese: ピッチャーは{緩急|かんきゅう}を{使|つか}い{分|わ}けてバッターを{抑|おさ}えた。
examples.english: The pitcher kept the batter in check by mixing slow and fast pitches.

examples.japanese: {緩急|かんきゅう}の{際|さい}には{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.english: Please contact us in case of emergency.

examples.japanese: {緩急|かんきゅう}を{要|よう}する{事態|じたい}に{備|そな}える。
examples.english: To prepare for situations requiring urgent action.

examples.japanese: {緩急|かんきゅう}{自在|じざい}にボールを{操|あやつ}る。
examples.english: To control the ball freely with varying speeds.
examples.notes: 緩急自在 means having complete control over pace variation

examples.japanese: {緩急|かんきゅう}あれば{助|たす}け{合|あ}うのが{仲間|なかま}だ。
examples.english: True friends help each other in times of need.

notes:
Composed of {緩|かん} (slow, relaxed) + {急|きゅう} (fast, urgent). The two senses come from different readings of this contrast: variation in speed (sense 1) versus the urgent end of the spectrum (sense 2).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {緩急|かんきゅう}をつける: to vary the pace
- {緩急|かんきゅう}{自在|じざい}: having complete control over pace variation
- {緩急|かんきゅう}の{際|さい}: in case of emergency
- {緩急|かんきゅう}を{使|つか}い{分|わ}ける: to mix fast and slow skillfully

USAGE BY DOMAIN:
- Music: varying tempo for expressiveness
- Baseball: mixing fast and slow pitches
- Speech/writing: varying rhythm and pacing

Sense 1 (pace variation) is far more common in modern usage. Sense 2 (emergency) appears mainly in formal or literary expressions like {緩急|かんきゅう}の{際|さい} and {緩急|かんきゅう}あれば.
